text: I was raised inside the temple.
My grandmother was the previous priestess.
The temple has always maintained the Song.
The Song is performed during important ceremonies.
Nobody in the temple understands the language of the Song.
My grandmother claimed the words are older than the village.
As a child I experienced vivid dreams after sleeping near the monument.
Those dreams stopped many years ago.
My grandmother believed dreams were messages from the ancestors.
I do not know whether she was right.
The Night of Ash happened when I was very young.
I remember adults being frightened.
For several months after the Night of Ash, the temple remained open day and night.
Many villagers prayed constantly during that period.
The monument has chambers that remain sealed.
No priestess in living memory has entered them.
A story says the founders swore an oath beneath the monument.
Nobody remembers the exact oath.
The Song contains a repeated phrase. My grandmother treated that phrase with special importance.
She refused to explain why.
The small ancient building near the monument contains carvings unlike any found elsewhere in the village.
Ren has copied some of those carvings.
I worry he will discover things better left forgotten.
Tarek's family possesses an heirloom older than any chief.
My grandmother once called it: 'The Companion of the Song.' She never explained what she meant.
